nodes.label: R2 presigned capability model
nodes.author: Cloudflare
nodes.rationale: R2 presigned URLs are bearer tokens, so Storvia must issue them short-lived and operation-scoped rather than treating them as ordinary links.

nodes.label: Google Drive file scope
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: The narrow drive.file scope is preferred because it limits access to files created, opened, or shared with the app and avoids broader restricted scopes.

nodes.label: Drive resumable upload protocol
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: The protocol provides a session URI, Content-Range progress, and recovery inspection; clients must not assume a lost response means no bytes were accepted.

nodes.label: OAuth state and redirect integrity
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: Random server-side state, exact redirect matching, backend-held secrets, and clean post-callback redirects reduce CSRF, replay, and code exposure risk.

nodes.label: Drive changes cursor
nodes.author: Google for Developers
nodes.rationale: A stored start page token and post-processing cursor advance provide efficient, recoverable change detection without replacing the ownership database.

nodes.label: RFC 9457 error shape
nodes.author: onurcinar
nodes.rationale: A standard application/problem+json body avoids forcing each client to learn a private error envelope.

nodes.label: ServeMux routing benchmark
nodes.author: rosgluk
nodes.rationale: The cited benchmark found the standard library router competitive while reducing dependencies, and the database dominates the request budget anyway.

nodes.label: Metrics implementation status
nodes.rationale: Prometheus metrics are implemented and served by the running binary, with families focused on routing, outcomes, bytes, jobs, and state.

nodes.label: Reconciliation status
nodes.rationale: Reconciliation is implemented, but Drive's outcome remains honestly unknown where the session capability is not retained.

nodes.label: Ambiguous provider write risk
nodes.rationale: A lost response may hide a successful write; same-provider reconciliation is safer than retrying into another location.

nodes.label: False outage classification risk
nodes.rationale: Quota, auth, policy, or validation failures must not be mistaken for availability failures because that would send data to fallback against policy.

nodes.label: No independent backup risk
nodes.rationale: The design is unsuitable where recovery after Drive loss, company-controlled immutable retention, or seamless reads during a Drive outage is required.

nodes.label: Go SDK recorded-location reads
nodes.rationale: Downloads and deletes follow the stored provider location, so a current outage does not authorize trying another provider.

nodes.label: Go SDK uncertain outcome
nodes.rationale: Transport failure is treated as possible prior processing; the safe response is reconciliation with the same key, never a new upload.

nodes.label: Go SDK provider upload modes
nodes.rationale: The server selects Drive session or S3 presigned parts, and the client must not influence the provider choice.

nodes.label: TypeScript SDK fallback disclosure
nodes.rationale: The client exposes whether fallback stores outside Drive so the UI can disclose that consequence rather than implying Drive-only storage.

nodes.label: TypeScript SDK reconciliation result
nodes.rationale: Only nothing_stored guarantees a restart is safe; unknown means the upload may exist and must not be duplicated.

nodes.label: TypeScript SDK recorded-location access
nodes.rationale: After recovery, fallback files remain read and deleted from the recorded fallback location; a provider outage is surfaced rather than transparently redirected.

nodes.label: TypeScript SDK upload helper
nodes.rationale: The helper completes either direct provider path and reports the Drive file ID because Storvia deliberately does not retain the Drive session.

nodes.label: Accepted no-copy limitations
nodes.rationale: Loss of the only file, fallback stay-in-place behavior, and same-provider uncertain outcomes are documented trade-offs rather than vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: Capability leakage risk
nodes.rationale: Drive session URIs, signed URLs, authorization codes, and raw provider bodies are bearer or sensitive material and must stay out of logs and unintended responses.

nodes.label: Tenant isolation risk
nodes.rationale: Identity must come from the authenticated session and provider pointers, keys, endpoints, and tenant IDs must never be trusted from browser input.

nodes.label: High-severity security scope
nodes.rationale: Tenant isolation, secret handling, OAuth integrity, single-location behavior, injection, capability leakage, and SDK idempotency are treated as security-critical surfaces.

nodes.label: Private vulnerability disclosure
nodes.rationale: Security reports should use private GitHub reporting, with a minimal public fallback only when the private channel is unavailable.

nodes.label: Live Drive verification status
nodes.rationale: The status record says Drive OAuth, folder creation, upload, read-back, delete, and outage routing have been verified against a real account/provider path.

nodes.label: Research source limitations
nodes.rationale: Provider behavior and community evidence can change or be anecdotal, so real file types, users, account mixes, and regions still require validation.

nodes.label: Pilot go or no-go gate
nodes.rationale: A limited pilot requires real controlled Drive and S3/R2 smoke tests plus evidence for isolation, idempotency, reconciliation, and no duplicate locations.

nodes.label: Pre-release verification status
nodes.rationale: The document explicitly withholds a production-readiness claim until live Google, S3/R2, PostgreSQL, and security review gaps are closed.

nodes.label: Pinned Next.js release exceptions
nodes.rationale: The exact Next.js and platform SWC releases are excluded from minimum release age gating to keep the pinned toolchain installable.

nodes.label: Disable sharp native builds
nodes.rationale: The console serves no images, so denying sharp's native build avoids an unnecessary native toolchain requirement.

nodes.label: Health-gated service startup
nodes.rationale: The API waits for healthy Postgres and Redis, and the distroless health check uses the binary's configuration validation because no shell or curl exists.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL local development stack
nodes.rationale: Development intentionally runs PostgreSQL rather than SQLite so dialect differences in leases, identifiers, and booleans are exercised before production.

nodes.label: Redis shared session and circuit state
nodes.norm_label: redis shared session and circuit state
nodes.rationale: Redis is included to exercise multi-instance shared access-token and Drive circuit state before it is required in production.

nodes.label: Redis live verification gap
nodes.rationale: Redis-backed sessions are implemented but have only been exercised through a failing stub, not a real Redis round trip.

nodes.label: Drive change-log poller status
nodes.rationale: The poller advances a Drive change cursor against a live account, while provider changes remain distinct from the ownership database.

nodes.label: S3 and R2 compatibility drift
nodes.rationale: The adapter must stay within the common S3 subset and verify behavior against the selected provider instead of assuming AWS features exist everywhere.

nodes.label: Go SDK stable idempotency key
nodes.rationale: A stable key makes retries safe; a fresh key would create a second provider write.

nodes.label: TypeScript SDK stable idempotency key
nodes.rationale: The browser client preserves the same duplicate-prevention contract as the Go SDK.

nodes.label: Durable documentation record
nodes.rationale: Each meaningful change must record decisions, behavior, actual checks, omissions, and next steps for future sessions.

nodes.label: Failure classification and single-location rules
nodes.rationale: A timeout does not prove a write failed, so routing must distinguish uncertainty from pre-write availability failure.

nodes.label: Configuration secret boundary
nodes.rationale: Checked-in JSON must contain ordinary settings only; actual credentials belong in ignored environment injection and no secret-reference field is allowed.

nodes.label: Drive-first storage direction
nodes.rationale: The project has confirmed Google Drive as the normal location and an S3-compatible provider only as an outage fallback, with no application-managed duplicate copies.

nodes.label: Next.js agent rules
nodes.rationale: The console's Next.js version may have breaking changes, so implementation work must consult the version-resolved guides and preserve the generated rule block.

nodes.label: Provider adapter boundary
nodes.rationale: Adapters own HTTP, credentials, signing, status parsing, and normalization; routing consumes normalized failure classes rather than raw provider responses.

nodes.label: Load-bearing storage contract
nodes.rationale: Routing behavior must be changed in the pure policy package and its table-driven tests must continue to mirror the documented failure matrix.

nodes.label: Structural enforcement principle
nodes.rationale: Constraints that cannot be bypassed by future callers are preferred over advisory checks in handlers or reviews.

nodes.label: Verification honesty rule
nodes.rationale: Documentation must distinguish commands actually run from planned checks and distinguish mocked paths from live-provider verification.

nodes.label: Runtime-only container secrets
nodes.rationale: Compose passes only credentials through environment injection while ordinary database and Redis settings remain in JSON configuration.

nodes.label: Testing console status
nodes.rationale: The console backend and live R2 behavior are verified, while browser interaction remains explicitly unverified.

nodes.label: Job workers and leases status
nodes.rationale: Workers and leases are implemented and a real job claim-and-complete cycle was observed.

nodes.label: Live R2 verification status
nodes.rationale: The fallback adapter and console path are recorded as verified against real Cloudflare R2, including upload, HeadObject verification, read-back, and deletion.
